newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds test resistance on rate talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds test resistance on rate talk.

text.p: Speculation of a further easing in monetary policy following today's Reserve Bank board meeting saw the bond market end just above last week's yield lows.

The December 10-year bond futures contract met strong resistance at 92.995 for the third time in just over week, leaving the benchmark 10-year bond yield straddling 7.0 percent for most after the afternoon session.

Offshore buying, a solid technical outlook after a corrective sell-off late last week, and speculation of a third possible easing in official interest rates this year fuelled the bullish tone, traders said.
While economists give only the slimmest chance of an easing after today's Board meeting, the recent strength of the local dollar has raised market expectations.

"Cutting rates again in the near term would not represent a third easing in monetary policy -- it would be more a case of trying to enforce the second easing," said Rory Robertson, interest rate strategist at Bankers Trust Australia.
He felt that a third easing would simply be an attempt to move conditions back in line the policy stance the RBA thought was justified on November 6.

The currency built on its recent strong advance, hitting a new six year high of US$0.8212 and a four year peak of over 93 yen in offshore trading on Monday. However, it has since been in correction, ending 2/3 U.S. cent lower by the local close.
Whether the central bank is concerned about the vitality of the dollar, politicians were out in force debating the issue.
Treasurer Peter Cosetello said that while the dollar will help keep inflation low, it will make it hard for import-competing parts of the economy.
However, he said the government is not targetting a particular level for the currency.
The Australian Laor opposition, meanwhile, was calling for a rate cut to offset the effects of the currency.

All eyes will be focused on the Reserve Bank's dealing intentions at 9.30 a.m. (2230 GMT), the usual time of day policy changes are announced, but this will quickly revert to the third quarter GDP report two hours later.

Although economists have raised their expectations for GDP following Monday's stronger than expected business investories, with the median now at a 0.9 percent rise, the annual growth should fall markedly. Forecasts centre on a year-on-year rate of 3.4 percent compared with 4.5 percent in the July quarter.

Bond yield spreads to other dollar bloc bonds remained tighter on the day, extending Monday's outperformance, and breaking through resistance at 100 basis points on the 10-year spread to the U.S. In Tokyo, Treasury yields were little changed after ending stable in New York.
